D.C. Metropolitan Police Department Interim Police Chief Jeffery Carroll said early Monday that a suspect with a weapon was struck when National Guard members responded to a street fight. (WJLA)

A repeat offender accused of shooting a National Guard member in Washington, D.C., as troops tried to break up a street fight had previously been convicted of assaulting police officers and illegally carrying a gun, federal officials said.

The U.S. Marshals Service on Monday identified Jerrell Jackson, 41, as the suspect in the shooting, which happened at about 11:15 p.m. Sunday in the 400 block of 8th Street SE.

Jackson was previously convicted of two counts of assault of a police officer and one count of carrying a pistol without a license and had three parole violations, the agency said.

NATIONAL GUARD MEMBER SHOT IN DC, POLICE CHIEF SAYS

Court records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Jackson has faced at least 13 prior criminal cases or arrests in the District dating back to 2004, involving allegations ranging from gun and drug offenses to assault, threats and unlawful entry. Some cases resulted in convictions, while others were dismissed or resolved through diversion.

Jerrell Jackson, 41, was identified as the suspect accused of shooting a National Guard member as troops tried to break up a street fight in Washington, D.C. (White House)

"We are praying this National Guard member has a quick and speedy recovery," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The suspect in the shooting has a lengthy rap sheet including two counts of assault of a police officer, illegally carrying a pistol, and multiple parole violations."

The National Guard member was shot in the leg and has since been released from the hospital.

DC GUARD SHOOTING SUSPECT STARES DOWN DEATH PENALTY IN FIRST COURT APPEARANCE

A fight broke out between at least two men outside a local business before National Guard members stepped in. At least one of the men then opened fire.

National Guard members returned fire, hitting Jackson in the abdomen, according to the U.S. Marshals Service.

100-SHOT SOMALI GANG GUN BATTLE ROCKS MINNESOTA AS SHERIFF WARNS 'WE'RE IN TROUBLE'

Jackson was taken to another hospital for treatment.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

National Guard members move through the area following the shooting of two National Guard soldiers near the White House Wednesday, Nov. 26, 2025, in Washington. (Mark Schiefelbein/AP)

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Investigators recovered a gun in an alley next to the shooting scene, along with at least 14 shell casings. No other suspects were at large, and no other National Guard members or civilians were injured.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

The U.S. Marshals Service and National Guard said they would not identify the wounded Guard member because of privacy concerns and the ongoing investigation.

SEND US A TIP

The shooting comes as the Trump administration touts the work of the D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force, which brings together more than 20 federal and local agencies along with the National Guard.

TRUMP'S DC CRIME CRACKDOWN 'WORKING' AS CITY SEES HOMICIDES PLUMMET 43% SINCE 2025: SLAIN INTERN'S MOM

National Guardsmen patrol the District of Columbia in 2026. (Mandel Ngan/Getty Images)

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

The task force has made more than 18,000 arrests, seized nearly 2,200 illegal guns and returned 28 missing children home, the U.S. Marshals Service said.

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

Bis credited the task force with driving down violent crime in the nation's capital.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Thanks to the President's Safe and Beautiful Task Force violent crime in the city has drastically decreased," Bis said. "D.C. residents and visitors are thankful for all the Task Force has done to drive down crime and make our nation’s capital safe again."

Fox News Digital’s Alex Nitzberg contributed to this report.
